Great game design. 10/10 would recommend.

Minimalistic and well made puzzle game. Love the subtle horror elements and the backrooms-esque vibe the game gives. 10/10, would really like a hard mode with some new more subtle anomalies, as well as making anomalies more subtle
Mild horror element at times but generally just a creepy vibe. Especially if the dude starts staring at you STOP DOING THAT

Me and my husband LOVED this! And We're gearing up to play Platform 8 this weekend. I hope you guys keep making stuff like this. It's the perfect game for sitting down for an hour or two with a friend, or loved one. Trying to spot the differences if there is one. A handful of fun surprises, ranging from creepy to fun. Definitely give this a shot and support the creators! Super affordable ;)
Gotta get out here, gotta exit. Got out first try (somehow) but is a great game with lots of things to replay.

Fantastic game. Went into it knowing nothing about it and that was definitely the way to go. I can't imagine how different the experience would have been otherwise. Highly highly recommend. You can finish it in one sitting and it's dirt cheap. Just play it.
A very clever take on spot the difference with a minor horror twist. I would love a game of puzzles just like this!

The Exit 8 is a nice spot the differences game, with a deep Japanese horror feel. I played it with one of my friends. We took turns exploring the area with the other player acting as a second set of eyes. After failing for over an hour to complete a run, we broke out a guide with a list of anomalies. There was one listed anomaly we had never noticed (to our probable detriment), but the main use of the guide was showing that the anomaly spawn points were finite. Limiting the level of details we paid attention to greatly sped up our hallway investigations.

First-person game with repetitive tile background, so potential nausea warning may apply. Nicely creepy, and low on outright scares.

This brings the traditional "find the differences" game to a next level. The atmosphere is good, especially when playing with earphones. Besides, Unreal Engine makes it looking very nice.

The hints are designed reasonably well, and the variety is rich. The value in playing multiple times after completion is not high, but it is still enjoyable to play it once a month, I think.

The hazard that frustrates me mostly is ... (I don't want to give a spoiler). But remember, we can run instead of walk by pressing "SHIFT" button after pressing "W" or "S" button. That is, we can only run after we walk ("W" is walking forward and "S" is walking backward).

If you want to be looking at the tiles on the ground and go "Is that off?" for 60 minutes, this is the game for you.

In all seriousness, this game is FUN, rewarding, and has that charm of PUNISHING you for YOUR mistakes. There are some anomalies that you will genuinely miss if you are NOT paying attention, though there are those ones that will make you pause, look at it, and go "Nope" and immediately turn around like Steven Universe's father. The game asks you to pay attention, so you better. From hard to notice, to in your face, this game is a great taste of the horror anomaly games. Strong recommend, and I heard there is a movie based off this game? I will have to check that out, but if you want a fun small game that you can replay for fun, I recommend this title. Heck, I think your partners might enjoy it alongside you if you have those partners who are pick up on things fast. Overall, a good time and worth the purchase.
i 100% this game so fast, i could have done it 3 times and still be able to get a refund, but i wont because the game is good.
A well made, tightly executed conceptual demo. Lots of fun to go through on a Friday night with others.
A short, unique, and interesting game. It’s actually surprising that a real movie was made based on a small indie game.

While being responsible for a explosion of fan games due to it's relatively novel concept, Exit 8 is very bland after the first 20 minutes or so. Of course it's still a very interesting game to play for the first time and absolutely worth it at a lower price, but the ever repeating white hallways begin to hurt your eyes after your 50th loop.

The movie did manage to do an amazing job adapting this simple game to the large screen, and I'll absolutely remember this game as time goes on.
This was a fun game with a few jumps along the way. I'm going to be seeing anomalies everywhere I go now...

I wish Steam had a maybe option for reviews. I feel like it wasn't very worth it for me because I'm good at this kind of stuff and beat it in 10 minutes. I will say though that the audio design was amazing.

This is finally a good horror game. WE FINALLY HAVE GAMES!!

The game was really well made; from the graphics, to the gameplay and the litte tricks the game is trying to sneak on you. It is one of the best horror games I have ever played and I mean it. I would like to see another version of Exit 8 someday. I bet many other people would like it too!

This was actually really cool, it surprised me multiple times. It is totally worth its price as its a short game, After seeing all anomalies, I can say there's not much repeatability unless you want to watch someone who hasn't seen it before play.

I decided to check this game out on a whim. Mostly because I like horror games and things that are unsettling. I wanted something with that whole "backrooms" feel/liminal spaces vibe. This delivers if you dig liminal spaces. If you've ever watched the TV show "Severance" that is what this game feels like. 

My first few play-throughs it was all about finding every last anomaly. Once I found all the anomalies I thought I would be done and that would be it - a nice little game a spent a few bucks on that I would maybe revisit every now and again. Quite the opposite. This has become my new favorite comfort game. It's easy to turn my brain off and just enjoy the atmosphere of "The Exit 8"

I would recommend this game most for people who enjoy walking simulators, some weirdness, a little bit of the uncanny, and don't mind redundancy in their games.
Like Platform 8, this one's price is a little steep for only up to an hour's worth of gameplay, but the anomalies are fun to discover and experience. Get both on sale, and try the VR one too!
I like this game, makes you really think about what's in front of you and makes you rethink and make you go crazy.

Ehhhhhh right on the line on if I recommend or not. I made it all the way to hallway 8 on my first run, was feeling clever for seeing the subtle tricks, but I missed something and got reset. I spent the next 20 minutes not getting past the 4th hallway, and found myself becoming very grateful for the super obvious anomalies which meant I could just move right on to the next test.

Fun? A little at first but quickly becomes frustrating as you have to go slower and slower it seems through every hallway, and the normal ones become almost annoying because it gives you anxiety about continuing on instead of turning back.

I'd rather do this kind of spot-the-difference in a magazine where there's no reward (i.e. end scene) being kept from you.

But the game is well done for what it is.
Clean and Simple. A fun kind of horror that does not require violence, gore, or an immense time-sinking effort. Just the sound of your foot steps, and the things that deviate from that.

Delivers on its premise. Short and sweet, liminal and creepy, and had me second guessing my eyes and my computer the entire time. The dev recently added more anomalies, and you're shown a list of undiscovered anomalies upon completing the game, which is right up my completionist alley. Will definitely dive back into this.

A word of caution: though this isn't really a 'jumpscare' type game (there is no non-diegetic sounds or music, for example, only sounds from within the world itself), there are some anomalies that can make you jump. One time, all the lights went out as I was rounding a corner , and while that isn't very scary in and of itself, I was hyper alert for any minute changes in my environment, so it scared the crap out of me, lol.

Brilliant little game!

Some of the anomalies are hidden REALLY well. Took me some time to finally beat the game! But it was a lot of fun. Can get a bit frustrating at times when you keep missing things, but you just need to look very very closely ;)
I don't really it get it. I didn't have fun. It barely seems like a game.

Was chased by a dude disguised as the subway tiles, a river of blood, twins, and a business man
8/8

Are you old enough to remember playing Flash horror games on Newgrounds and the like? Think less "jumpscares" and more "escape the room" type stuff and you've got a decent idea what this is like. It's not very scary, but I suppose it's a bit creepy in places. Mostly it's a casual stroll down a weird hallway. Is that worth $3 to you? It was for me. I think it does a good job at what it does, but what is does is pretty limited. Don't get it if you're looking for a narrative or jumpscares. Do get it if you want a nice, kinda creepy hallway-walker. It costs less than a McDonald's cheeseburger right now, and you'll probably enjoy this more.

its surprisingly fun. a nice little game you can break out when someone is over to laugh about and count posters. If I was trying to play it alone i might feel differently, but it still does a really good job of making you paranoid about doorknobs and subway tiles.
this game was hard for me because i don't know how to count, so i never knew if i was close to winning.
This game will have you second guessing your life decisions quicker than ever. Would play this game again

very cool. you never know what type of whacky stuff you're gonna see. one time i got shrunk down to joe rogan height. another time a big ol' tidal wave came at me and i had to run away.

A short and fun anomaly-spotting game. It has some eerie elements, but no crazy jump scares. Played it on Steam Deck, and it works great!

Was about to uninstall until I took the time to read what the game is about and then I finally understood how to play and it was like a fun game of I, Spy minus the limbo like state I was trapped in,

good game but very short depending on how well you notice tiny details,your luck and how good your memory is but overall is a good horror-ish experience
Cool little game of eye spy the liminal horror. About an hour if you're okay at it. It's fun. Worth the $5.

This game will make you slowly descend into madness as you scrutinize every little detail. Unless you're like me and you can't handle even a grain of horror so you scrutinize everything off the bat
Very short but very fun, it's only 4$ (and can be even be under 3$ on sale) so even if you solve it quickly it's not more than the price. And if you want more gameplay you can find all the anomalies :D

(SPOILER FREE) A very good psychological horror game where you explore the underground passageway to find a way out, I think this game is really good when you know how it works however it can be a bit confusing at times especially if you missed the instructions like I did, but overall this is a great game to buy if you have some extra cash left over.
good thing train stations and passageways are not actually this creepy in Japan because I'd never set foot there again

I recently played "The Exit 8" with my wife, and we both had a great time. Though it was quite short and it didn't take us long to discover all the anomalies, It has this eerie charm to it. From its liminal space aesthetic to its subtly creepy vibes, the game left a lasting impression with its immersive atmosphere and attention to detail.

Very short, however, I liked the concept. Some of the anomalies I couldn't detect and ended up being chance. I couldn't tell if I was hearing or seeing them or they were so subtle that my brain didnt pick up on them.
Awesome game, add more differences or more rooms u can choose from as DLC :o)

I was disappointed in this game. I thought it was going to be a lot more exploration, but the game takes place in a very small space. Even after accepting the game for what it is, I still found the game to be too fickle in determining whether or not I managed to turn back quick enough after spotting an anomaly.

The game is short but cool and i do think its worth the price of $4 or get it on sale. Unlike that other guy, i dont mind with the time "wasted" lookin for anomalies, it's a damn puzzle you have to solve. As for replay value not much there, i think its cool if you let ya homies or fam mess with the game so you can watch their reaction and hear them complain about "why am i back on 0?"

After playing a similar game, many people in my community recommended The Exit 8 with high marks. My expectations were, rightfully so, a little higher than normal. This game was way more difficult than the other similar game I played, but this is not to say it is a negative. You really have to look everywhere in this hallway for anomalies! Some of them are certainly super obvious, but those can certainly feel uneasy, just to make the game a bit more "horror" rather than a sci-fi. Certainly worth the price tag, especially if you didn't find every anomaly and are a completionist.

If you beat this game in less than 2 hours and refund it anyways, you are a piece of sh!t.

Basically all you need is to tell the difference and make the decision. Require much patience and discernment.
The weird feeling that the game creates keep you captured all the time. It's not really a horror game though I think, but the tense and depressed environment is the essence.
Pretty cool. I liked it despite the struggle and finding out I missed quite a few after beating it :]

If you're observant you can finish this game in minutes.
If not, you'll be there for hours, or more.
Who knew a single repetitive hallway could be so creepy

The game is really fun to play, and also quite scary at times. The movement and sound design is fantastic and feels really smooth and well done. It is not an easy game but also not unnecessarily difficult. Can make for a fun time, and for a price that cheap you're almost guaranteed to have a good deal!
